en: The Apadāna of the Elder Ñāṇasaññika Sereyyavagga, Chapter 8 I was a merchant’s son in the city of Benares, and my name was Nāgasena. At that time, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, was dwelling at the foot of the Ajapāla banyan tree after having just attained enlightenment. Having heard that the Blessed One had become enlightened, I went to him with great joy. Having approached the Blessed One, I paid homage to him and sat down to one side. As I sat there, the Blessed One, out of compassion for me, taught me the Dhamma by means of a progressive discourse: he spoke on generosity, on virtuous conduct, and on heaven; he revealed the peril, the vanity, and the defilement of sensual pleasures, and he proclaimed the blessings of renunciation. When the Blessed One knew that my mind was ready, pliable, free from hindrances, joyful, and confident, he then revealed to me the Dhamma teaching of the Buddhas, which is the beginning of the state of Nirvana. Just as a clean and stainless cloth absorbs dye properly, even so, while I sat right there, the stainless, immaculate eye of the Dhamma arose within me: "Whatever is subject to origination is all subject to cessation. Then, having seen the Dhamma, having attained the Dhamma, having known the Dhamma, having penetrated the Dhamma, having crossed over doubt, having transcended uncertainty, having gained fearlessness, and having become independent of others in the Teacher's dispensation, I rose from my seat, prostrated myself with my head at the Blessed One's feet, and said: "Excellent, O Blessed One! Excellent, O Sugata! Just as one might set upright what was overturned, or reveal what was hidden, or show the way to one who was lost, or bring an oil lamp into the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms, even so has the Dhamma been made clear by the Blessed One in many ways. I go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the Dhamma, and to the Sangha of Bhikkhus. May I receive the going-forth in the presence of the Blessed One, may I receive ordination! The Blessed One granted me the going-forth; the Sublime One ordained me. And not long after my ordination, while still a novice, I dwelt in a forest thicket near the city of Benares. There, I applied myself to meditation on the perception of knowledge (*ñāṇasaññā*). By constantly and repeatedly practicing this perception of knowledge, I attained the state of an Arahant. I have fulfilled the duties of a monk, lived the holy life, done what was to be done, and laid aside the burden. I have attained my own goal, destroyed the fetters of existence, and through right gnosis, I am liberated. My mind is released from the taints through the realization of liberation. I am now a Worthy One (*Arahant*), cool and possessed of final Nibbāna. By this truthful word, may I be successful in every way. Through this truth, may I be established in the attainment of the fruit of Arahantship. May I be one who possesses the sixfold supernormal power and the threefold knowledge. “I dwell upon a mountain in the Himalayas, in the midst of the mountains;
having seen a beautiful sandy bank, I thought:”
I recollected the Best of Buddhas.
There is no comparison for his wisdom;
there is no equal to the Teacher’s conditioned formation.
Having directly known all phenomena,
one is resolved through wisdom.
Homage to you, O noble steed among men!
Homage to you, O Supreme among Men!
There is no one equal to you in wisdom,
for your wisdom is supreme throughout all that exists.
Having gained confidence in my mind through knowledge,
may I rejoice in heaven for an eon;
and for the remaining eons, may I likewise rejoice.
A wholesome deed was performed by me.
Ninety-one aeons ago,
that merit which I then obtained—
I do not know a state of woe;
this is the fruit of my perception through knowledge.
In the seventy-first aeon from now,
One was Pulinapupphiya;
he was a wheel-turning monarch of great power, endowed with the seven treasures.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Ñāṇasaññika spoke these verses.
This is the eighth legend of the elder Ñāṇasaññika.
